notes: Existing integration: accredited programs whose required course titles join the two topics in one course; programs teaching it as two courses: accredited programs whose titles carry the topics in separate courses. Potential further integration: the 81 modeled programs that teach a pair as two courses, where the model may merge it; soils with foundations shows integration but no modeled program teaches it apart. The merging assumption, that a merged course keeps the larger credit of the two and the topics of both, belongs to the model and is not evidence of equivalent learning; Table S4 sets it against course descriptions. A course joins at most one merged course: where two pairs compete for one course (15 courses in 11 programs, for example a methods course with materials and with equipment), the pair that more programs teach as one comes first, so no credit is counted twice.

notes: Means over the 81 modeled programs at the binding count. The scenarios are alternatives, not all 90-credit degrees: the last rows give the mean totals and the programs that reach 90. In both scenarios the listed general education courses and electives are not deleted as knowledge: the model replaces them with the general education credits needed to meet the applicable count, together with the mathematics, science and economics courses kept and the construction hours counted as general education, which lie within the construction rows and add no credits. Components may not sum to the totals because of rounding.
